CLI native defaults are .junie/skills with separate .agents readers. Project overrides user for duplicate native names; compatibility duplicate precedence remains unverified.

Project .agents skills require a trusted project. Default roots can be disabled via --skill-default-locations, JUNIE_SKILL_DEFAULT_LOCATIONS or configuration. Additional skill locations, extension/built-in skills and enabled state are not modeled or modified.

Environment variables, Configuration files (https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/environment-variables.html; updated 2026-10-15, reviewed 2026-10-16) names JUNIE_HOME as home storage, but the reviewed skills sections do not establish its exact replacement skill roots. JUNIE_HOME relocation remains unverified and is not interpreted as a skills write override.

Config documentation (https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli-configuration.html; reviewed 2026-10-16), Project trust, describes temporary project storage for untrusted interactive projects. This installer does not grant trust or target transient host-managed storage.

The skills introduction mentions IDE support, but its path sections specify CLI. AI Assistant 2026.2 Agents (https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/agents.html; updated 2026-10-07, reviewed 2026-10-16) does not list native Junie skills as supported. Native IDE/plugin and CLI-via-ACP discovery remain separate version/surface gaps; no IDE target is enabled.
Cursor/Claude/Codex directories are described as import candidates, not default readable roots. No import/migration is performed and no fork path or state-home override is inherited.

Only canonical directory-form skills with general-spec metadata are installed. The host optional-description convenience does not weaken validation. No additional reserved local name or minimum skills version is established.
Skill location provides macOS/Linux and Windows home examples. Native copying does not prove host discovery, activation, trust or a validated installed version.

Machine-local/default readers only; host configuration may disable compatibility/global roots. Native Windows is not a documented CLI host; WSL is not a native Windows path mapping.

Getting Started With the CLI (https://ampcode.com/docs/cli), reviewed 2026-10-16, explicitly supports macOS, Linux and Windows through WSL. Native Windows is rejected, despite Windows configuration examples elsewhere; WSL requires a Linux process/context and remains untested as a host.

Preferred writes follow documented project .agents/skills and machine-local --global ~/.config/agents/skills. User scope means machine-local files, not publishing to the personal hosted skills repository. Project placement can coincide with Codex and must retain both target attributions.

Ordinary local readers preserve their relative precedence: ~/.config/agents, ~/.agents, ~/.config/amp, project .agents, project .claude and ~/.claude, each with skills suffix. Project parent searches are documented without a precise bound in the reviewed skills page, so exact root descriptors do not assert a repository boundary.

Claude plugin caches, additional amp.skills.path entries, personal/workspace hosted repositories, active plugins and official built-ins are not enumerated or used as write destinations. Recursive discovery up to five levels is host behavior, not a resolver scan.

Configuration (https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/settings), reviewed 2026-10-16, documents default-false disableClaudeCodeSkills and disableGlobalAgentsSkills. The installer does not parse settings, grant trust, change enablement or guarantee that a copied skill is active.

No XDG_CONFIG_HOME, AMP_HOME, AMP_CONFIG_DIR or other host relocation is inferred from generic configuration names or --settings-file. Extra paths are additional configuration, not a native write replacement.

Skills, MCP Servers in Skills states that Amp connects to skill MCP servers on discovery. Copying does not run or connect anything; later host discovery can execute commands or access networks and is not a safety guarantee. No host was launched.

General portable validation remains required. No additional reserved local name or minimum skills version is established. IDE, macOS/iOS app, Puck, orb/runner, hosted and remote variants remain separate unverified/excluded capabilities.

Host-owned README documentation at revision d65d6850ca4ed4971e4cb1a3bebd960a79cc167b is the authority, not implementation source or a third-party installer. Features and Installation explicitly identify macOS/Linux and native Windows PowerShell.

Preferred project placement is documented .crush/skills; preferred user placement chooses the documented common XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crush/skills root, falling back only when absent to explicit home/.config/crush/skills. The Windows installation example uses LocalAppData instead; the global-reader list says Windows also reads those paths, not that common roots stop applying.

Windows-only LOCALAPPDATA agents/crush roots and USERPROFILE/AppData/Local fallbacks are additional readers not enumerated by this adapter. They are not inferred as replacement write roots or applied to Unix. The common documented root is an installer choice, not a claim of platform-preferred host order.

CRUSH_SKILLS_DIR and options.skills_paths are additional readers, not documented replacements for all global discovery. They are not interpreted as write overrides. CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG and CRUSH_GLOBAL_DATA do not establish a skills relocation rule in the reviewed text.

XDG relocates the documented agents/crush global readers; independent ~/.agents and ~/.claude readers stay under explicit home, so all-reader resolution still requires home. Empty/relative/tilde XDG values are rejected by strict installer policy, not claimed host behavior.

Read list order is not evidence of duplicate precedence. Exact root descriptors do not scan ancestors, nested skills or custom configuration; duplicate precedence, extra reserved local skill names and minimum skills version remain unverified.

Host disabled-skills and invocation settings remain unchanged. crushrc is executable Bash configuration; the installer neither reads/evaluates it nor launches Crush. Strict portable validation/no-link copy remains mandatory; copied skill scripts never run.

Android, BSD, IDE, remote and other architecture/filesystem hosts remain outside native validation. Real-host discovery, activation and installed versions are untested; successful copying is not a sandbox or host-discovery guarantee.
